topics.title: Perimeter and the mystery ratio π

learn.hook: Measure round a bangle, a plate and a tyre with a thread, divide by the width each time... and get the same number!
points: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary of a closed shape.
For a composite figure, add the lengths of all the straight parts and curved parts on the outside only, not the lines inside.
For every circle, circumference ÷ diameter is the same constant, called π ≈ 3.14159...

People approximated π over centuries: Mesopotamians used about 3⅛; Archimedes trapped it between 223/71 and 22/7 using 96-sided polygons; Liu Hui got about 3.1416; Zu Chongzhi found 355/113; Aryabhata gave 3.1416; Brahmagupta used √10.

example.q: A window is a 1.4 m by 1 m rectangle topped by a semicircle on the 1.4 m side. Find its perimeter. (π = 22/7)
steps: Straight parts: 1 + 1.4 + 1 = 3.4 m (the top side is replaced by the arc)

learn.reallife: Fencing a garden shaped like a rectangle with a round end needs exactly this composite perimeter.

games.title: Who used which value of π?
Perimeter check
items: The perimeter of a shape includes lines drawn inside it.
Only the outer boundary counts.
C ÷ d is the same for a coin and for the Earth's equator.
It is π for every circle.
355/113 is very close to π.
It equals 3.1415929..., correct to 6 decimal places.
Archimedes used polygons inside and outside a circle to estimate π.
He went up to 96 sides.
π is exactly 3.
It is about 3.14159.

quiz.q: What is π defined as?
quiz.explain: For every circle this ratio is the same constant, π.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the radius

quiz.q: Sneha wraps a thread around a tin and finds the circumference is 31.4 cm. Its diameter is 10 cm. What ratio does she get?
quiz.explain: 31.4 ÷ 10 = 3.14, an approximation of π.
quiz.mistake: Divides the diameter by the circumference

quiz.q: A shape is a square of side 7 cm with a semicircle on one side (diameter 7 cm), outside the square. What is its perimeter? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Three square sides 21 cm plus the semicircle 11 cm; the side under the semicircle is not on the boundary.
quiz.mistake: Includes the side covered by the semicircle

quiz.q: Which value did Zu Chongzhi give for π?
quiz.explain: 355/113 = 3.1415929..., remarkably accurate.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up with Archimedes' upper bound 22/7

quiz.q: How did Archimedes estimate π?
options: Using regular polygons inside and outside a circle
Measuring a thread around a pot
quiz.explain: With 96-sided polygons he showed 223/71 < π < 22/7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks he used Madhava's series

quiz.q: Brahmagupta used √10 for π. Is √10 bigger or smaller than π?
quiz.mistake: Assumes ancient values were always too small

quiz.q: A running track is a rectangle 100 m by 60 m with semicircles on both 60 m ends. What is the perimeter of the track? (π = 3.14)
quiz.explain: Two straights 200 m plus two semicircles of diameter 60, which make one full circle: 3.14 × 60 = 188.4 m.
quiz.mistake: Includes the 60 m ends as well as the semicircles

quiz.q: Which of these is the most accurate approximation of π?
quiz.mistake: Thinks 22/7 is the best because it is the most common

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What is π and how did people find it?"
teach.praise: Fantastic! π is circumference ÷ diameter, and many mathematicians approximated it!
teach.nudge: What do you divide by what to get π? Can you name someone who estimated it?

learn.hook: A round rangoli, a cricket ground, a bangle: circles are everywhere. Just one number, the radius, decides their size!
points: Circumference (perimeter) of a circle: C = 2πr = πd, where r is the radius and d the diameter.
Area of a circle: A = πr². We often use π = 22/7 or 3.14.
A semicircle has perimeter πr + 2r (the curved part plus the diameter).
Area of a ring (between circles of radii R and r): π(R² − r²).
A sector with central angle θ has area (θ/360) × πr².

example.q: Meena draws a circular rangoli of radius 21 cm. Find the length of its border and its area. (Use π = 22/7.)

learn.reallife: The distance a bicycle moves in one turn of its wheel equals the wheel's circumference. That is how a cycle's odometer counts kilometres.

items.text: The perimeter of a semicircle is πr + ___
If the radius doubles, the area becomes ___ times as big

quiz.q: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.mistake: Uses πr (forgetting the 2) or confuses circumference with area

quiz.q: A circular flower bed has radius 21 m. What is its area? (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.mistake: Uses 2πr (the circumference) instead of πr²

quiz.q: A bangle has diameter 7 cm. What is the length of the bangle around? (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.mistake: Treats the diameter as the radius and doubles again

quiz.q: A cycle wheel has radius 35 cm. How far does the cycle move in 10 complete turns of the wheel? (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.explain: One turn = 2 × 22/7 × 35 = 220 cm. Ten turns = 2200 cm = 22 m.
quiz.mistake: Makes a mistake converting centimetres to metres

quiz.q: A ring-shaped path lies between two circles of radii 14 m and 7 m. Find the area of the path. (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.mistake: Uses π(R − r)², which gives 154

quiz.q: Find the perimeter of a semicircular protractor of radius 7 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.explain: Perimeter = curved part + straight edge = πr + 2r = 22 + 14 = 36 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the straight diameter

quiz.q: The circumference of a circular plate is 44 cm. What is its area? (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.explain: 2πr = 44 gives r = 7 cm. Then A = 22/7 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm².
quiz.mistake: Takes 44 as the diameter or radius instead of solving for r

quiz.q: A round pizza of radius 21 cm is cut into 6 equal slices. What is the area of one slice? (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.explain: Each slice is a sector with central angle 60°, which is 1/6 of the circle. 1/6 × 1386 = 231 cm².
quiz.mistake: Gives the whole pizza's area, or divides by 12

teach.ask: Gappu has a round roti: "How do I find the length around it and the space it covers? Are they the same thing?"
teach.praise: Around the roti is the circumference 2πr; the space it covers is the area πr². Two different things! Yum.
teach.nudge: Which formula gives the length around the edge, and which gives the space inside?

learn.hook: 22/7 is a great guess, but π never ends and never repeats. Not even a supercomputer can finish writing it!
points: π cannot be written as p/q with integers p and q; its decimals go on forever without repeating.
22/7 = 3.142857... and 3.14 are only approximations; 22/7 is slightly bigger than π, and 3.14 slightly smaller.
Madhava of Sangamagrama (Kerala, about 1400 CE) found π/4 = 1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − 1/7 + 1/9 − ...; the partial sums swing above and below π/4 and slowly settle down.
Pi Day is 14 March (3/14) and Pi Approximation Day is 22 July (22/7).

example.q: Find 4 × (1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − 1/7). Is it above or below π?

learn.reallife: Students celebrate Pi Day on 14 March with π-recitation contests and round foods like rotis and pizzas.

games.title: Exact or approximate?
items: Circumference ÷ diameter

items.text: Madhava's series has odd ___ with alternating signs.

quiz.q: Which statement about π is true?
options: π cannot be written as a fraction of two integers
π's decimal repeats after six digits
quiz.explain: π is irrational: its decimal neither ends nor repeats.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the school value 22/7 is exact

quiz.q: Is 22/7 greater or less than π?
quiz.explain: 22/7 overshoots π by about 0.0013.
quiz.mistake: Assumes approximations are always smaller

quiz.q: Which is Madhava's series?
quiz.explain: It uses odd denominators with alternating signs and sums to π/4.
quiz.mistake: Uses all whole numbers

quiz.q: Find 4(1 − 1/3) as the first estimate from Madhava's series.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply by 4
Adds all terms instead of alternating

quiz.q: Why is Pi Approximation Day on 22 July?
options: 22/7 is a well-known approximation of π
July is the 7th month and π ≈ 7
quiz.explain: Written day/month, 22/7 matches the fraction.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with Pi Day 3/14

quiz.q: The partial sums of Madhava's series (×4) go 4, 2.67, 3.47, 2.90, 3.34, ... What do they do?
options: Swing above and below π, getting closer
quiz.explain: Adding and subtracting smaller and smaller terms makes them zigzag around π.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sums move in one direction

quiz.q: Kunal measures a circle and gets C/d = 3.15. What does this show?
options: His measurement has a small error; π is still 3.14159...
quiz.explain: π is the same for all circles; measurements can only approximate it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks π depends on the circle

teach.praise: Correct! 22/7 is only close; π is irrational and its decimals never end or repeat!
teach.nudge: Is 22/7 exact or just close? What kind of number is π?

learn.hook: A slice of pizza has two straight edges and one curved crust. How long is the crust?
points: Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr for a central angle θ in degrees.
Perimeter of a sector = arc length + 2r (two radii).
Shapes built from semicircles and quarter circles: add up each curved piece. A flower made of semicircles on the sides of a square has perimeter = 4 × (semicircle arcs).
Circumference is proportional to radius, so if two circles' perimeters are in ratio 3 : 5, their radii are also 3 : 5.

example.q: Find the perimeter of a sector of radius 21 cm and angle 60°. (π = 22/7)

learn.reallife: The crust of a pizza slice is an arc, and decorators trimming fan-shaped cards need the sector perimeter.

quiz.q: Find the arc length for a central angle of 45° in a circle of radius 28 cm. (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Uses πr² instead of 2πr

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a quadrant (quarter circle) of radius 14 cm? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Arc = ¼ × 88 = 22 cm; add two radii 28 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the two radii

quiz.q: A sector of radius 10 cm has arc length 15 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Perimeter = 15 + 2 × 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds only one radius

quiz.q: A flower design has four semicircles drawn outwards on the sides of a square of side 14 cm. What is the perimeter of the flower? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Each semicircle has radius 7: arc = 22 cm. Four of them: 88 cm. The square's sides are inside.
quiz.mistake: Adds the square's sides as well

quiz.q: The perimeters of two circles are in the ratio 4 : 9. What is the ratio of their radii?
quiz.explain: C = 2πr, so C is proportional to r.
quiz.mistake: Takes square roots as for areas

quiz.q: Two circular tracks have circumferences 132 m and 220 m. What is the radius of the smaller one? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Divides by π only, getting the diameter

quiz.q: A shape is made of two quarter circles of radius 7 cm placed back to back to make an S-curve. How long is the curve? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Each quarter arc = ¼ × 44 = 11 cm; two make 22 cm.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one arc

quiz.q: An arc of a circle of radius 9 cm is 6π cm long. What is its central angle?
quiz.mistake: Uses the area formula

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I find the length of the crust of one pizza slice?"
teach.praise: Yummy maths! Take the angle's fraction of 2πr, and add 2r for the full perimeter!
teach.nudge: What fraction of the whole circle is the slice? What do you multiply that fraction by?

learn.hook: Two rectangles with the same fence length can hold very different numbers of cows!
points: Same perimeter does not mean same area: 1 × 9 and 5 × 5 rectangles both have perimeter 20, but areas 9 and 25.
Same area does not mean same perimeter: 1 × 16 and 4 × 4 both have area 16, but perimeters 34 and 16.
But two rectangles with the same area AND the same perimeter must be congruent: l + b and l × b fix l and b.
On a running track, outer lanes are longer on the bends, so starting lines are staggered: for one lap the extra is 2π × (lane width) per lane.

Staircase paradox: replace the diagonal of a 3 × 4 rectangle by a staircase. However tiny the steps, the staircase length stays 3 + 4 = 7, never reaching the diagonal's 5. Looking similar does not mean equal length.

example.q: On a 400 m track, lanes are 1.25 m wide. How much further ahead should a runner in lane 2 start than lane 1 for a one-lap race? (π = 3.14)
steps: The two bends make one full circle
Lane 2's circle has radius 1.25 m more

learn.reallife: Race officials paint staggered starting lines on school sports tracks using exactly this calculation.

games.title: Same perimeter 24 cm: which has bigger area?
Puzzle facts
items: Rectangles with equal perimeters always have equal areas.
1 × 9 and 5 × 5 differ.
Two rectangles with equal area and equal perimeter are congruent.
The sum and product of the sides fix both sides.
Outer lanes start ahead because their bends are longer.
A bigger radius gives a longer arc.
A staircase with very tiny steps has length equal to the diagonal.
It keeps the length of the two sides.
Among rectangles with perimeter 20, the square has the largest area.
5 × 5 = 25 is the maximum.

quiz.q: A rectangle and a square both have perimeter 36 cm. The rectangle is 12 cm long. Which has the larger area?
quiz.explain: Rectangle: 12 × 6 = 72. Square: side 9, area 81.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal perimeters give equal areas

quiz.q: A rectangle has area 36 cm² and sides 2 cm and 18 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: 2(2 + 18) = 40, much more than a 6 × 6 square's 24 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides only once

quiz.q: Rectangle A is 4 × 6. Rectangle B has the same area 24 and the same perimeter 20. What are B's sides?
quiz.explain: l + b = 10 and lb = 24 have only the solution 4 and 6. Equal area and perimeter force congruence.
quiz.mistake: Picks a pair with the same area but different perimeter

quiz.q: On a track with lanes 1.2 m wide, by how much is one lap in lane 3 longer than in lane 1? (π = 3.14)
quiz.explain: Lane 3 is 2 lanes out: 2π × 2.4 = 15.072 m.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one lane width

quiz.q: Why do runners in outer lanes start ahead in a 400 m race?
options: Their bends have bigger radius, so a lap in their lane is longer
quiz.explain: Straights are equal; only the curved parts differ.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the straight sections differ

quiz.q: A 6 × 8 rectangle's diagonal is replaced by a staircase of 100 tiny steps. How long is the staircase?
quiz.explain: Horizontal parts add to 6 and vertical parts to 8, whatever the step size.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the staircase approaches the diagonal length 10

quiz.q: For the same rectangle, what is the diagonal length?
quiz.explain: √(36 + 64) = 10, shorter than the staircase's 14.
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides

quiz.q: Among all rectangles with perimeter 40 m, which has the largest area?
quiz.explain: For a fixed perimeter the square gives the most area: 100 m².
quiz.mistake: Thinks a longer rectangle encloses more

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "If two gardens have the same fence length, do they have the same area?"
teach.praise: Exactly! Same perimeter can give different areas, and the square holds the most!
teach.nudge: Can a long thin rectangle and a square have the same perimeter? Do they hold the same area?

learn.hook: A farmer in Punjab wants to sow wheat on an odd-shaped field. Break it into triangles and rectangles, and its area is no longer a mystery!
points: Perimeter is the length of the boundary; area is the amount of surface inside, measured in square units such as cm² or m².
Triangle: area = ½ × base × height, where the height is perpendicular to the base.
Parallelogram: area = base × height. Rectangle: length × breadth. Square: side².
Trapezium: area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × distance between them. Rhombus: area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ (product of diagonals).
Any quadrilateral can be split by a diagonal into two triangles; add their areas.

example.q: A field is a trapezium with parallel sides 30 m and 20 m, which are 12 m apart. Find its area.

learn.reallife: Painters, tile-layers and farmers all estimate costs by area: ₹ per square metre of paint, tiles or seeds.

items.q: Triangle: base 10 cm, height 6 cm. Area in cm²?
Parallelogram: base 7 m, height 5 m. Area in m²?
Rhombus: diagonals 6 cm and 8 cm. Area in cm²?
Square of side 12 cm. Area in cm²?
Trapezium: parallel sides 5 and 7, height 4. Area?
Rectangle 15 m by 4 m. Perimeter in m?

quiz.q: Find the area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 7 cm.
quiz.explain: Area = ½ × 12 × 7 = 42 cm².
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½ and gets 84

quiz.q: A parallelogram-shaped plot has base 15 m and height 8 m. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Area of a parallelogram = base × height = 15 × 8 = 120 m².
quiz.mistake: Uses ½ as for a triangle, or adds the sides

quiz.q: A rhombus-shaped kite has diagonals 10 cm and 16 cm. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 cm².
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the diagonals but forgets the ½

quiz.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 9 cm and 13 cm, and the distance between them is 6 cm. Find its area.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½, or uses only the longer parallel side

quiz.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, diagonal AC = 20 m. The perpendiculars from B and D to AC are 6 m and 8 m. Find the area of ABCD.
quiz.explain: AC splits ABCD into two triangles with base 20 m: ½ × 20 × 6 + ½ × 20 × 8 = 60 + 80 = 140 m².
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½ for each triangle

quiz.q: A rectangular garden has perimeter 36 m and length 10 m. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Length + breadth = 36 ÷ 2 = 18, so breadth = 8 m. Area = 10 × 8 = 80 m².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to halve the perimeter, so takes breadth as 26

quiz.q: A right triangle has legs 9 cm and 12 cm. What is its area?
quiz.explain: In a right triangle the two legs are perpendicular, so one is the base and the other the height: ½ × 9 × 12 = 54 cm².
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½

quiz.q: A triangle has area 60 cm² and base 15 cm. What is its height?
quiz.mistake: Divides 60 by 15 and forgets the ½ in the formula

teach.ask: Gappu has a strange four-sided field: "No formula fits my field. How can I find its area?"
teach.praise: Draw a diagonal to split it into two triangles, find each area with ½ × base × height and add. My field is measured!
teach.nudge: Can you cut the field into shapes you already know? Which shape is easiest?

topics.title: Same base, same parallels and medians

learn.hook: Push the top of a parallelogram sideways like a deck of cards: its shape changes but its area doesn't!
points: Area pictures prove identities: an a × a square with a b × b corner removed rearranges into an (a + b) × (a − b) rectangle, so a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels have equal area, because they have the same base and the same height.
Triangles on the same base and between the same parallels have equal area (½ × base × same height).
A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. It splits the triangle into two triangles with equal bases and the same height, so equal areas.

example.q: Triangle ABC has area 48 cm² and AD is a median. Find the area of triangle ABD.
steps: Triangles ABD and ADC share the height from A

learn.reallife: Farmers dividing a triangular plot fairly between two children can draw a median.

games.title: Equal area?
items: Two parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels have equal area.
Same base and same height.
A median divides a triangle into two congruent triangles.
Equal areas, but not necessarily the same shape.
A triangle and a parallelogram on the same base and between the same parallels have equal area.
The triangle has half the parallelogram's area.
Triangles with the same base and equal heights have equal area.
½ × b × h is the same.
(a + b)(a − b) with a = 99, b = 1.

items.q: Parallelogram 50 cm², triangle on same base and parallels
All three medians drawn in a 72 cm² triangle: one of the 6 small triangles
Triangle on same base, area 18; another between same parallels

quiz.q: Parallelograms ABCD and ABEF are on the same base AB and between the same parallels. ABCD has area 56 cm². What is the area of ABEF?
quiz.explain: Same base and same height give equal areas.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the slant changes the area

quiz.q: Triangle PQR and parallelogram PQST are on the same base PQ and between the same parallels. The parallelogram has area 40 cm². What is the area of the triangle?
quiz.explain: The triangle has half the parallelogram's area.
quiz.mistake: Thinks they are equal

quiz.q: In triangle ABC, AD is a median and the area of ABD is 17 cm². What is the area of ABC?
quiz.explain: The median splits the area equally.
quiz.mistake: Halves instead of doubling

quiz.q: Why does a median split a triangle into two equal areas?
options: The median is perpendicular to the base
Both parts have equal bases and the same height
quiz.explain: Base BD = DC and both triangles have the height from A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the median must be an altitude

quiz.q: Triangles ABC and ABD lie on the same base AB, with C and D on a line parallel to AB. Area of ABC is 30 cm². Area of ABD?
quiz.explain: Same base and same height.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the triangles must be congruent to have equal area

quiz.q: Use the area picture of a² − b² to find 75² − 25².
quiz.mistake: Subtracts first and squares: 50²

quiz.q: A square of side 12 cm has a square of side 5 cm cut from one corner. The L-shape is rearranged into a rectangle. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract the cut-out square

quiz.q: In triangle ABC, median AD is drawn, then median BE of triangle ABD (E is the midpoint of AD). If ABC is 80 cm², what is the area of ABE?
quiz.explain: ABD = 40 (half of ABC). BE is a median of ABD, so ABE = 20.
quiz.mistake: Halves only once

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Why do slanted and straight parallelograms on the same base have the same area?"
teach.praise: Perfect! Same base and same height mean the same area!
teach.nudge: What stays the same when you slide the top? Think about the base and the height.

learn.hook: Over 1900 years ago, Heron of Alexandria found a way to get a triangle's area from its three sides alone. No height needed!
points: Heron's formula is used when you know all three sides a, b, c of a triangle but not its height.
First find the semi-perimeter: s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.
Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)].
For an equilateral triangle of side a, this gives area = (√3/4) × a².
A quadrilateral with a known diagonal can be split into two triangles, and Heron's formula used on each.

example.q: Find the area of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm.

learn.reallife: Surveyors measuring a triangular plot of land can easily measure the three sides with a tape, but not the height across the middle. Heron's formula is perfect for them.

games.title: Heron step by step
items: Measure the three sides a, b and c
Find s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2
Work out s − a, s − b and s − c
Multiply s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)
Take the square root to get the area

quiz.q: What is the semi-perimeter of a triangle with sides 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm?
quiz.mistake: Gives the full perimeter instead of half of it

quiz.q: Use Heron's formula to find the area of a triangle with sides 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take the square root at the end

quiz.q: Find the area of a triangle with sides 9 cm, 10 cm and 17 cm.
quiz.mistake: Stops before taking the square root

quiz.q: Find the area of an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm, correct to two decimal places.
steps: s = 15, s − a = 5 for each side
quiz.mistake: Uses ½ × side × side as if the height equalled the side

quiz.q: An isosceles triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Uses ½ × 5 × 6 = 15, taking a slanted side as the height

quiz.q: A triangular park has sides 40 m, 24 m and 32 m. Grass costs ₹5 per m². What is the cost of grassing the park?
quiz.mistake: Gives the area as the cost, or forgets the ½ when finding s

quiz.q: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and its perimeter is 36 cm. Find its area.
quiz.explain: The sides are 9, 12 and 15 cm. s = 18, area = √(18 × 9 × 6 × 3) = √2916 = 54 cm².
steps: One part = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 cm, so sides are 9, 12, 15
quiz.mistake: Forgets the square root, or doubles the answer

quiz.q: When is Heron's formula most useful?
options: When the base and height are known
When all three sides are known but the height is not
quiz.explain: Heron's formula needs only the three side lengths, so it works for any triangle when the height is unknown.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Heron's formula only works for special triangles

teach.ask: Gappu measured the three sides of a triangle with string but has no idea of its height: "Can I still find the area?"
teach.praise: Yes! Halve the perimeter to get s, multiply s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c), and take the square root. Heron would be proud!
teach.nudge: What is s, and what do you do with it and the three sides?

learn.hook: Double the sides of a photo and you need four times the paper. Area grows faster than length!
points: Join the midpoints of the sides of any quadrilateral: the inner quadrilateral (a parallelogram) has exactly half the area of the original.
In a parallelogram, any triangle with one side of the parallelogram as base and its third vertex on the opposite side has half the parallelogram's area.
In a square, joining midpoints, diagonals or a vertex to a midpoint creates pieces whose areas are simple fractions of the whole (½, ¼, ⅛ ...).
Scaling: if all lengths are multiplied by k, area is multiplied by k². So doubling lengths makes the area 4 times.

example.q: A square has side 10 cm. Its side midpoints are joined. Find the area of the new square.
steps: Midpoint figure has half the area

learn.reallife: Map makers know that a map at half the scale shows each region with only a quarter of the area.

items.text: Triangle on a side of a parallelogram with vertex on the opposite side = ___
A diagonal cuts a square into two parts, each ___
Both diagonals cut a square into 4 triangles, each ___

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has area 64 cm². What is the area of the quadrilateral formed by joining the midpoints of its sides?
quiz.explain: The midpoint quadrilateral always has half the area.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is one quarter, as for midpoint triangles

quiz.q: ABCD is a parallelogram of area 90 cm². P is any point on side CD. What is the area of triangle ABP?
quiz.explain: Same base AB and same height as the parallelogram, so half its area.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the area depends on where P is

quiz.q: A square of side 8 cm. E is the midpoint of side BC. What is the area of triangle ABE?
quiz.explain: Legs AB = 8 and BE = 4: ½ × 8 × 4 = 16, which is ¼ of 64.
quiz.mistake: Uses the full side for BE

quiz.q: A triangle's sides are all tripled. Its old area was 12 cm². What is the new area?
quiz.explain: Area scales by 3² = 9: 12 × 9.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the area by 3

quiz.q: A photo of 10 cm × 15 cm is enlarged so that each side is 2.5 times as long. How many times as much area does the print have?
quiz.explain: Area factor = 2.5² = 6.25.
quiz.mistake: Uses the length factor for the area

quiz.q: A map's scale is changed so that all lengths become half. A district covered 36 cm² before. What does it cover now?
quiz.mistake: Halves the area

quiz.q: Two similar plots have areas 25 m² and 100 m². What is the ratio of their corresponding sides?
quiz.explain: Area ratio 1 : 4 means length ratio √1 : √4 = 1 : 2.
quiz.mistake: Takes the area ratio as the length ratio

quiz.q: The midpoints of the sides of a rectangle 12 cm × 8 cm are joined. What shape and area does the inner figure have?
quiz.explain: Its diagonals are 12 and 8 and are perpendicular: area ½ × 12 × 8 = 48, half of 96.
quiz.mistake: Assumes the inner shape is also a rectangle

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "If I double every side of a shape, does the area double too?"
teach.praise: Correct! Doubling lengths multiplies area by 2², which is 4!
teach.nudge: When lengths become k times, what happens to area? Try a 1 × 1 square doubled.

topics.title: Brahmagupta's formula and squaring a rectangle

learn.hook: Ancient altar-builders had to make a square with exactly the area of a rectangle. Baudhayana showed how!
points: Brahmagupta's formula: a cyclic quadrilateral with sides a, b, c, d has area √((s − a)(s − b)(s − c)(s − d)), where s = (a + b + c + d)/2.
If one side shrinks to zero (d = 0), the quadrilateral becomes a triangle and the formula turns into Heron's: √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)).
Identity behind squaring a rectangle: ab = ((a + b)/2)² − ((a − b)/2)².

Baudhayana's method (Sulba Sutras): cut a b × b square from an a × b rectangle, split the leftover strip into two halves and move one half to another side, forming a big square of side (a + b)/2 missing a small square of side (a − b)/2. Then Pythagoras gives a single square with the same area.

example.q: Find the side of a square with the same area as a 9 m × 4 m rectangle using the identity.

learn.reallife: Vedic altar builders (vedi) followed the Sulba Sutras to change shapes while keeping area exactly the same.

games.title: Squaring a 9 × 4 rectangle
items: Cut a 4 × 4 square from the rectangle
Split the leftover 5 × 4 strip into two 2.5 × 4 strips
Move one strip to the side to make a 6.5 × 6.5 square missing a 2.5 × 2.5 corner
Use Pythagoras: side² = 6.5² − 2.5² = 36
The equal square has side 6

quiz.q: A cyclic quadrilateral has sides 7, 15, 20 and 24 m. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Uses s = 66 (the full perimeter)

quiz.q: A cyclic quadrilateral has sides 6, 6, 8 and 8 cm (a kite with two right angles). Find its area using Brahmagupta's formula.
quiz.explain: s = 14; (8)(8)(6)(6) = 2304; √2304 = 48. (It is two 6-8-10 right triangles of 24 each.)
quiz.mistake: Forgets the square root

quiz.q: What happens to Brahmagupta's formula if side d becomes 0?
options: It becomes the area of a rectangle
It becomes Heron's formula for a triangle
quiz.explain: With d = 0, s − d = s, giving √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)).
quiz.mistake: Thinks the area must vanish

quiz.q: Which identity lets us turn a rectangle into an equal square?
quiz.explain: A product equals a difference of two squares, and a difference of squares is one square by Pythagoras.
quiz.mistake: Uses an identity that is not true

quiz.q: Find the side of the square with the same area as a 16 cm × 4 cm rectangle.
quiz.explain: Area 64, so side √64. Check: 10² − 6² = 64.
quiz.mistake: Averages the sides

quiz.q: For a 12 × 3 rectangle, what is the side of the big square in Baudhayana's L-shape?
quiz.mistake: Uses (a − b)/2

quiz.q: For the same 12 × 3 rectangle, what is the side of the equal-area square?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the sides instead of the squares

quiz.q: Who described a method for converting a rectangle into a square of equal area?
quiz.explain: The Sulba Sutras give construction rules for altars, including this one.
quiz.mistake: Credits Brahmagupta, whose formula is for cyclic quadrilaterals

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How can I make a square with exactly the same area as a rectangle?"
teach.praise: Wonderful! Write ab as a difference of two squares and use Pythagoras, like Baudhayana!
teach.nudge: Which identity writes ab using two squares? How does Pythagoras help?

topics.title: Why πr², segments and swept areas

learn.hook: Slice a roti into many thin wedges, flip every other one, and the circle turns into a rectangle!
points: Cut a circle into many equal sectors and lay them alternately up and down: they form an almost-rectangle of length πr (half the circumference) and height r, so area = πr². Indian texts such as those of Nilakantha Somayaji describe this rearrangement.
Archimedes showed the circle has the same area as a right triangle with legs r and 2πr: ½ × r × 2πr = πr².
A segment is the region between a chord and its arc. Minor segment area = sector area − area of triangle OAB; major segment = circle area − minor segment.
Area swept by a clock hand or a wiper blade is a sector: (θ/360) × πr²; for a wiper whose blade starts some distance from the pivot, it is the difference of two sectors.

example.q: Find the area of the minor segment cut off by a chord that subtends 90° at the centre of a circle of radius 14 cm. (π = 22/7)

learn.reallife: Car designers calculate the area a wiper clears so drivers can see the road in heavy monsoon rain.

games.title: Rearrange the circle
items: Cut the circle into many equal sectors
Place them alternately pointing up and down
They form a shape close to a rectangle
Its length is half the circumference, πr, and its height is r
Area = πr × r = πr²

quiz.q: In the rearrangement of sectors into a near-rectangle, what is the length of the rectangle?
quiz.explain: Half the sector arcs are on top and half on the bottom, so each long side is half of 2πr.
quiz.mistake: Uses the whole circumference

quiz.q: Archimedes compared a circle to a right triangle with legs:
quiz.explain: ½ × r × 2πr = πr².
quiz.mistake: Uses the diameter as a leg

quiz.q: A chord subtends 60° at the centre of a circle of radius 6 cm. The triangle OAB has area 9√3 ≈ 15.59 cm². Find the minor segment area. (π = 3.14)
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract the triangle

quiz.q: In a circle of radius 14 cm, a 90° chord's minor segment is 56 cm². What is the major segment area? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Circle area = 616; major segment = 616 − 56.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the sector instead of the minor segment

quiz.q: A clock's minute hand is 14 cm long. What area does it sweep in 5 minutes? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Uses 5/60 of the circumference instead of the area

quiz.q: A car wiper blade of length 21 cm is attached at one end and sweeps 120°. What area does it clean? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Uses the arc length formula

quiz.q: A wiper's rubber blade runs from 7 cm to 21 cm from the pivot and sweeps 90°. What area does the rubber clean? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Big sector ¼ × 22/7 × 441 = 346.5; small sector ¼ × 22/7 × 49 = 38.5; difference 308.
quiz.mistake: Uses only the outer sector

quiz.q: What is a segment of a circle?
options: The region between two radii and an arc
The region between two concentric circles
The region between a chord and its arc
quiz.explain: A sector uses two radii; a segment uses a chord.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a segment with a sector

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Why is the area of a circle πr²?"
teach.praise: Amazing! Slices rearranged into a rectangle πr long and r high give πr²!
teach.nudge: What shape do the rearranged slices make? What are its length and height?

topics.title: Polygons in circles and shaded regions

learn.hook: A square inside a circle covers about 64% of it, a hexagon about 83%. More sides, closer to the circle!
points: A square inscribed in a circle of radius r has diagonal 2r, so its area is 2r²; ratio to the circle = 2/π ≈ 0.64.
An inscribed equilateral triangle has area (3√3/4)r²; ratio ≈ 0.41. An inscribed regular hexagon has area (3√3/2)r²; ratio ≈ 0.83.
As the number of sides grows, the inscribed polygon fills more of the circle.
For shaded regions, write shaded area = (big shape) − (pieces removed), or add pieces. Four quarter circles at the corners of a square make one full circle together.

example.q: A circle is drawn inside a square of side 14 cm, touching all four sides. Find the area outside the circle but inside the square. (π = 22/7)

learn.reallife: Tile designs with circles in squares need shaded-area calculations to order the right amount of each colour of marble.

games.title: Inscribed in the same circle
items: Equilateral triangle
Square
Regular hexagon
Circle itself

items.q: Square 14 with 4 corner quadrants r = 7: shaded
Circle r = 7, inscribed square: square area

quiz.q: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 10 cm. What is the area of the square?
quiz.explain: Its diagonal is the diameter 20 cm; area = d²/2 = 400/2.
quiz.mistake: Uses the radius as the side

quiz.q: What fraction of a circle's area does an inscribed square cover?
quiz.mistake: Uses the ratio for a square drawn around the circle

quiz.q: Which inscribed shape covers the largest part of a circle?
quiz.explain: Ratios: triangle ≈ 0.41, square ≈ 0.64, hexagon ≈ 0.83.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square is closest to a circle

quiz.q: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 2 cm. Using area = (3√3/2)r², its area is:
quiz.mistake: Forgets to square the radius

quiz.q: At each corner of a square of side 14 cm, a quarter circle of radius 7 cm is drawn inside. What area of the square is not covered by them? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Four quadrants of radius 7 make one circle of area 154. 196 − 154 = 42.
quiz.mistake: Adds four full circles

quiz.q: A circular park of radius 21 m has a square flower bed of side 14 m in the middle. What area is left for grass? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Adds the areas

quiz.q: Two semicircles of radius 7 cm are cut out from the two 14 cm sides of a 14 cm × 20 cm rectangle. What area is left? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Two semicircles of radius 7 = one circle of 154. 280 − 154 = 126.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts only one semicircle

quiz.q: A circle of radius 7 cm has an inscribed square. What is the area inside the circle but outside the square? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Square = 2 × 49 = 98; circle = 154; difference 56.
quiz.mistake: Uses the circumscribed square of side 14

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I find the area of a shaded part in a picture with circles and squares?"
teach.praise: Great! Find the whole, subtract the unshaded parts (or add the shaded pieces)!
teach.nudge: Which big area can you start with? What do you remove from it?
